text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky hails EU summit in Dublin as a breakthrough for making the first steps towards a common job policy in the European Union.

- German car maker BMW is looking to invest five billion schillings in a new plant. Upper Austrian town Steyr is thought to have a good chance of attracting the investment, with only one other contender, from Great Britain.
- Austria's energy industry sees potential for giving preference to national energy sources, even after the liberalisation of the market.
- Chamber of Workers wants the European Union and World Trade Organisation to create a counterweight against unwieldy transnational firms.
- "We are still the elite", SS-Veterans of World War II said, at their annual meeting in southern Austria at the weekend.
- Austrian Airlines have made an agreement to cooperate with Singapore Airlines.
- Far-right Freedom Party wants Austrians to have a say in granting Austrian citizenships to foreigners.
- "Is Austria to be a global player or a ball to be played with?", was the main question at a meeting of the Economic Forum of Executives.

- Finance Minister Viktor Klima and provincial treasurers have reached an agreement on funding hospitals next year. The government will pay up to six billion schillings for losses due to tax changes resulting from European Union membership.

- Former Finance Minister Hannes Androsch is still looking for partners to take over German tyre maker Continental's ailing Austrian unit Semperit. After talks with U.S. Goodyear, he is due to meet next with Italian Pirelli.
- Lack of risk capital is slowing down Austrian innovation. Financial experts say banks and government should rethink situation.
